correction.text: the Mahdist State of 1885-1888 without Suakin and Wadi Halfa (still Anglo-Egyptian) and without Equatoria (Emin Pasha's province, Mahdist only from 1889)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Mahdist shape begins in 1890. After the fall of Khartoum (26 January 1885) Kassala and Sennar fell, and 'Suakin and Wadi Halfa' were the only places still in Anglo-Egyptian hands in 1885; the 1890 shape is used without those two places. The page gives no area. The 1885 gain event 'the rest of the northern, eastern and central Sudan' carries everything this keyframe adds to the 1883 keyframe. Reviewer round: now 1885..1888 and without Equatoria: the Equatoria page (opened in the reviewer round) says 'The Mahdist Revolt put an end to Equatoria as an Egyptian outpost in 1889', that Emin 'had already been deposed as governor by his officers in August 1887' and that by late 1888 the Mahdists controlled the province; the Mahdist State page's 'begun to move into the southern region' by the end of 1885 is movement, not control.

correction.text: the Mahdist State of 1885-1889 without Suakin and Wadi Halfa, still Anglo-Egyptian

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (reviewer round): the 1885-1888 shape plus Equatoria, which the Mahdists held after the end of Emin Pasha's province in 1889 (Equatoria page: 'The Mahdist Revolt put an end to Equatoria as an Egyptian outpost in 1889'). Still without Suakin and Wadi Halfa.

2.33 M km2. The page gives no infobox area, so the area check is impossible; Sudan and South Sudan today total about 2.5 M km2, the same order. Reviewer fix: the shape reaches 22N (Wadi Halfa) and the Red Sea coast, but the Mahdist State page says 'In all of Sudan, only Sawakin, reinforced by Indian army troops, and Wadi Halfa on the northern frontier remained in Anglo-Egyptian hands' and neither page says the Ansar took either place later, so a 50 km disc around each is removed here as in the 1885 keyframe (and in 1895, 1898 and 1899). The shape also takes in the Equatoria fringe in Uganda and the DRC (about 50,000 km2): the Equatoria page puts the Mahdist control of the province at 1888-1889, while the Mahdist State page says 'The Belgians prevented the Mahdi's men from conquering Equatoria' (undated); the disagreement is not resolved.

ledger.note: 1881: Muhammad Ahmad proclaims himself the Mahdi at the start of the Mahdist War against Egyptian rule. The page: 'In 1881, Muhammad Ahmad proclaimed himself the Mahdi'; it names no place for the proclamation, so the core is read from the 1882 Al Ubayyid and Sheikan events (Kordofan). Fix fx-16: the Nuba Mountains (South Kordofan) stay the Kingdom of Taqali's until July 1884 (Kingdom of Taqali page); /ledger/3 brings them in.

region.text: Al Ubayyid and Sheikan, Kordofan, without the Nuba Mountains

ledger.note: 1882: the Ansar take Al Ubayyid and Kordofan. The Ansar 'defeated an Egyptian force' at Al Ubayyid and later 'an 8,000-man relief force at Sheikan'; the page gives no exact date for the Al Ubayyid capture. Fix fx-16: the Nuba Mountains are left out until /ledger/3 (Kingdom of Taqali page: still independent in July 1884).

region.text: most of Darfur

ledger.note: 1883: Darfur falls to the Mahdists. 'Mahdist forces soon took control of most of Darfur'; the governor Slatin 'was captured in 1883'. The page does not give the year of the surrender itself, so the region is read from Slatin's capture.

region.text: all of the Nuba Mountains, centred on the Taqali Massif (the Taqali dossier's region)

ledger.note: July 1884: the Mahdists take the Kingdom of Taqali. Kingdom of Taqali page (read 2026-11-01): "In July 1884 the ruler of Taqali, Makk Adam, was captured by the Mahdists and eventually died in captivity." and "The state was then conquered by the forces of the self-proclaimed Mahdi, Muhammad Ahmad, in the late 19th century."; regnal list "Interregnum 1884-1898". The Mahdist State page names neither Taqali nor the Nuba Mountains, so the extent (all the Nuba Mountains, drawn as South Kordofan) is the Taqali page's description of the state. Mirrors kingdom-of-taqali /ledger/3 (loss, July 1884). Added by fix fx-16 after the compiler found the Taqali and Mahdist outlines claiming the same land in 1881, 1883 and 1898.

region.text: Kassala and Sennar

ledger.note: 1885: Kassala and Sennar fall. 'Kassala and Sennar fell soon after' the fall of Khartoum.

1885: the Mahdists destroy Ottoman Khartoum and build a new capital at Omdurman. The page: 'The Mahdists destroyed Ottoman Khartoum, building a new capital across the river at Omdurman'; it gives no date, so the year is bridged from the fall of Khartoum on 26 January 1885 (page silent).

'by the end of 1885, the Ansar had begun to move into the southern region'; the page names no province, so the region is Cliopatria's 1890 shape in South Sudan (page silent on which provinces fell). Reviewer round: Equatoria is excluded; the Equatoria page puts the Mahdist control of that province in 1888-1889 (ledger 1889).

region.text: the 1885 keyframe less Kordofan and Darfur: Khartoum, the Gezira, Sennar, Kassala, the Blue Nile, the northern Nile valley to Dongola and Berber, the Red Sea hills and the south except Equatoria, Wadi Halfa and Suakin

ledger.note: 1885: the rest of the Egyptian Sudan falls to the Ansar. The page (re-read) names only Khartoum (26 January 1885), 'Kassala and Sennar fell soon after, and by the end of 1885, the Ansar had begun to move into the southern region', and then 'In all of Sudan, only Sawakin, reinforced by Indian army troops, and Wadi Halfa on the northern frontier remained in Anglo-Egyptian hands'. It names no Berber, Dongola, Gezira, Blue Nile or Red Sea hills event, so the year is the page's end-of-1885 state and the region is the reading that everything else was Mahdist by then (about 1.5 M km2 by grid cells, more than the single events above: the discs around Khartoum, Kassala and Sennar and the south). The Khedivate of Egypt shape for 1880-1884 (8,031 cells) still covers this land; Cliopatria's British Africa shape of 1885-1889 also covers it (8,627 of the 8,635 cells of the 1890 shape): the British Africa dossier (af-08) must trim the Sudan from its 1885 shape. Reviewer round: Equatoria is excluded (Egyptian outpost until 1889, see the 1889 gain).

region.text: Khartoum, the Ottoman-Egyptian seat

ledger.note: 26 January 1885: the Ansar take Khartoum. The infobox gives the fall of Khartoum as 26 January 1885, and the relief force arrived 'too late': 'the town had fallen two days earlier'.

region.text: Dembea and Gondar

ledger.note: January 1886: a Mahdist army invades Ethiopia. 'In January 1886, a Mahdist army invaded Ethiopia, seized Dembea'; 'in January 1888, the Mahdists returned, defeating Tekle Haymanot at Sar Weha and sacking Gondar'. Dembea is read as the Gondar lowlands. The Mahdist State page dates the 60,000-man invasion to 1887 (disagreement).

region.text: the Gondar frontier, left with the Ethiopians

ledger.note: 1889: the Ethiopian front closes after Gallabat. After Yohannes fell in the Battle of Gallabat the Ethiopians withdrew, and the war 'mostly wasted the Mahdists' resources'; no land changed hands.

region.text: Equatoria Province, Emin Pasha's Egyptian outpost: the Equatoria states of South Sudan and the Uganda and DRC fringe of the 1890 shape

ledger.note: 1889: Equatoria passes to the Mahdists. 'The Mahdist Revolt put an end to Equatoria as an Egyptian outpost in 1889'; Emin 'had already been deposed as governor by his officers in August 1887'; by late 1888 'the Mahdists controlled the province'. The year is the page's end of Equatoria; the extent is the researcher's reading (the South Sudan Equatoria states and the Uganda and DRC fringe of Cliopatria's 1890 shape). The Mahdist State page, by contrast, says 'The Belgians prevented the Mahdi's men from conquering Equatoria'.

region.text: Kassala

ledger.note: 1894: the Italians take Kassala. The Mahdists 'had lost [Kassala] to the Italians in 1894' after the Battle of Kassala (the infobox: 'Kassala temporarily occupied by Italy'). Cliopatria's 1895 shape still holds Kassala and is corrected.

region.text: the southern fringe lost between the 1890 and 1895 shapes

ledger.note: 1895: Cliopatria's shape loses 25,000 km2 in the south (22.9E-32.1E, 2.0N-10.9N). The pages opened give no date: 'The Belgians prevented the Mahdi's men from conquering Equatoria'. Region and year are the researcher's bridge from the shape change (page silent). Reviewer round, Lado Enclave page: the Congo State received the Lado area by the 1894 treaties (British-Congolese 12 May, Franco-Congolese 14 August), 'Leopold's expedition did not reach the enclave until 1896', 'Chaltin's forces reached the Nile at the town of Bedden in the enclave in February 1897' and 'took control in 1897'; the enclave measured about 39,000 km2. The page gives no date for the Mahdist loss of the area, so the dossier keeps Cliopatria's 1895 shape change (confidence 1); the Belgian take-over dated 1897 may be the better year (unresolved).

region.text: Dongola, the former capital of Nubia

ledger.note: September 1896: Kitchener takes Dongola. He 'captured the former capital of Nubia by September'.

region.text: all of the Nuba Mountains, centred on the Taqali Massif (the Taqali dossier's region)

ledger.note: 1898: the Mahdist hold on the Nuba Mountains ends with the restoration of the Makk. Kingdom of Taqali page (read 2026-11-01): regnal list "Interregnum 1884-1898" and Jayli ruling 1898-1916; "The Makk of Taqali was restored to power but remained closely controlled by the British." The page's text also says "In 1889 the Mahdists were defeated by the British, who formed Anglo-Egyptian Sudan", which clashes with its own table and with the Mahdist State page (Omdurman, 2 September 1898); 1898 is used. No month is given, so none is set; the event stands before the September events of the year. Mirrors kingdom-of-taqali /ledger/4 (gain, now with this state as counterpart). Added by fix fx-16.

region.text: Omdurman, the Mahdist capital

ledger.note: 2 September 1898: the Anglo-Egyptian army takes Omdurman. 'the Anglo-Egyptians reached Omdurman, the Mahdist capital, on 2 September' after the Battle of Atbara in April 1898; the Khalifa's 52,000-man frontal assault failed (Mahdist State page). The Nile valley between Abu Hamed and Omdurman is not dated by either page.

region.text: Darfur as it stood in 1873

ledger.note: September 1898: Darfur leaves the Mahdist State. Ali Dinar page (read 2026-11-01): infobox "Reign: September 1898 - 6 November 1916"; he "[r]endered hapless the Mahdist garrison at al-Fashir and rival contenders to the throne" (the page does not say when Mahdist rule ended, and dates the Battle of Omdurman nowhere); Sultanate of Darfur page (read 2026-11-01): infobox "Independence from the Mahdist State: 1898"; Ali Dinar "managed to re-establish Darfur's self-rule". Mirrors sultanate-of-darfur /ledger/10 (gain, September 1898, confidence 3 there; 2 here because neither page dates the Mahdist withdrawal). Added by fix fx-16.

The Anglo-Egyptians 'finally caught up with Abdullah at Umm Diwaykarat, where he was killed, effectively ending the Mahdist regime'; the Mahdist State page: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan, the Sudan Convention of 18 January 1899. region.text: the remnant of the Mahdist State

ledger.note: 24-25 November 1899: the Khalifa dies at Umm Diwaykarat and the Mahdist State ends. The infobox of the Mahdist State page gives 24 November 1899, the Mahdist War page 25 November 1899; a holdout at Kabkabiya under Sanin Husain lasted until 1909.

wars.name: Mahdist War

zones.text: Dembea and Gondar, invaded January 1886 and January 1888
Kassala, taken by the Italians in 1894
the Nile valley from Dongola to Berber, the 1896-1898 campaign

wars.outcome: Anglo-Egyptian victory: Omdurman falls on 2 September 1898, the Khalifa is killed at Umm Diwaykarat in November 1899 and Sudan becomes the Anglo-Egyptian condominium (Sudan Convention of 18 January 1899). The Mahdists lose Kassala to the Italians in 1894 and the Nile valley to Kitchener in 1896-1898.
wars.note: The Mahdist War page gives the war's infobox end as 25 November 1899. Fronts: Ethiopia (1886 and 1888; Gallabat, 1889), Egypt (Toski, 1889), Italian Eritrea (Agordat, December 1893; Kassala, 1894), Congo (the Belgians block Equatoria, undated; the Lado Enclave until 1910) and the Dongola Expedition (Ferkeh, 7 June 1896).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line fixes the Mahdist frontiers: Egypt at Wadi Halfa, Ethiopia near Gallabat, Italian Eritrea at Kassala, the Congo in Equatoria. All are approximate.

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages, two used. Cliopatria's Mahdist shape starts in 1890 although the Mahdi proclaimed himself in 1881 and took Khartoum in 1885: new keyframes 1881, 1883, 1885 cover 1881-1889 (the Khedivate of Egypt shape for 1880-1884 overlaps 1881-1884; the ledger's gains from khedivate-of-egypt carry the change). Between 1890 and 1895 the shape drops 25,000 km2 in the south without a dated page (ledger 1895, confidence 1); the 1895 shape keeps Kassala although Italy took it in 1894 (corrected); the 1898 shape keeps Omdurman after 2 September 1898 (new keyframe 1899). The Equatoria fringe in the DRC and Uganda (about 50,000 km2) of the 1890 shape is doubtful: the page says the Belgians prevented the conquest of Equatoria. Pages disagree on the Ethiopian invasion: January 1886 and January 1888 (Mahdist War) against 1887 with 60,000 men (Mahdist State). The page does not date the capital's move to Omdurman. Not on the pages: Fashoda (naval action of 25 August 1898 mentioned without a territorial result), the Darfur restoration under Ali Dinar after 1898, the Italian handover of Kassala. Counterparts needing dossiers: anglo-egyptian-sudan (the condominium, 1899-1956, successor), the restored Sultanate of Darfur under Ali Dinar, Equatoria Province of Emin Pasha. Gazetteer names needed: Abu Hamed, Suakin (places). Reviewer round (af-01-c-fixed): (1) the 1890 keyframe is now 'adjust' and, with the 1895, 1898 and 1899 corrections, removes Wadi Halfa and Suakin (50 km discs) because the page keeps them Anglo-Egyptian ('only Sawakin ... and Wadi Halfa ... remained in Anglo-Egyptian hands') and says nowhere that the Ansar took them. (2) A new 1885 gain (counterpart khedivate-of-egypt, confidence 2) carries the land the 1885 keyframe adds to the 1883 keyframe (Kordofan and Darfur): about 1.5 M km2 of the northern, eastern and central Sudan that no dated event named; the page gives only the end-of-1885 state. (3) The British Africa dossier (af-08) must trim the Sudan from its 1885-1889 shape: Cliopatria's British Africa 1885 shape overlaps 8,627 of the 8,635 cells of the Mahdist 1890 shape (no overlap from 1890), besides the Khedivate of Egypt overlap of 1881-1884 (8,031 cells). Reviewer round, thin items: the Equatoria page (opened) dates the end of Emin Pasha's Egyptian outpost to 1889 and the Mahdist control to late 1888-1889, so Equatoria (the Equatoria states of South Sudan and the Uganda and DRC fringe) is cut from the 1885-1888 keyframe, added by a new 1889 keyframe and a 1889 gain (counterpart 'Equatoria Province', confidence 2); the 'southern region' of 1885 stays at confidence 1 for the rest of South Sudan (the Bahr al-Ghazal, 1884, is on no page opened). The Lado Enclave page gives the Belgian take-over of the area as 1897 (Chaltin, Bedden, February 1897) against Cliopatria's 1895 shape change; unresolved. Still not reached: the Omdurman page (capital move), the Siege of Khartoum page (Berber, Osman Digna's east), the Battle of Umm Diwaykarat page (extent of the 1899 remnant), the Muhammad Ahmad page (El Obeid year). Counterpart needing a dossier: Equatoria Province (Emin Pasha, until 1889).
